author: Good Enough
description:
Tiny devices known as “pencil bombs” were used to sabotage ships during wartime.

These small time-delay tools were designed to be hidden aboard vessels and triggered hours later, causing critical damage without immediate detection. Despite their size, they played a role in covert operations aimed at disrupting enemy supply lines.

This Short explores how something so small could be used in large-scale sabotage during World War I.
